content.title: About
content.content: Chicken roll is a roasted piece of chicken breast rolled into a cylindrical shape and seasoned with spices. It has a tender flavor, aromatic spices, and a crisp outer crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Roasting retains most of the nutrients found in chicken meat.
Rolls are commonly used in fast‑food and as a convenient snack.
For a golden crust, rolls are often brushed with a light coating of breadcrumbs or flour.
Chicken is considered a leaner protein compared with beef or pork.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When roasted, the roll contains less fat than fried alternatives, making it suitable for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken is a good source of vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The roll supplies phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones and immune function.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor salmonella; proper cooking temperatures are essential.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt and sauces can raise sodium levels, which may be a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken roll can be enjoyed hot or cold, sliced into salads, sandwiches, added to pasta dishes, or served with a yogurt‑based dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the roll in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in an airtight container for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C.
